messages:
alana (DevEx): hitting a weird edge where async client.fn_call + structured_output triggers two backend tool requests. The second one has no auth header and then parsing fails. Can someone eyeball?

rory (Py SDK): Ugh. Can you drop a tiny repro and the failing HTTP dump?

alana (DevEx): minimal repro below (async):
```py
# repro_async.py
import os
import asyncio
from redwood import RedwoodClient

client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['RW_KEY'])

async def main():
    out = await client.fn_call(
        model='gpt-4.1',
        fn_name='lookup_user',
        fn_schema={"type":"object","properties":{"user_id":{"type":"string"}}},
        input='lookup 42',
        structured_output=True,
    )
    print(out)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    asyncio.run(main())
```

alana (DevEx): HTTP capture from my local run:
```
-> POST /v1/tools/lookup_user  Authorization: Bearer sk_test_abc  (200)
-> POST /v1/tools/lookup_user  Authorization:  (502)
```
The client then tries to parse the combined stream and hits `json.JSONDecodeError: Extra data`.

nina (QA): repro on macOS, py310, httpx 0.24.1. I see the same pattern. Looks specific to fn_call + structured_output in async mode; regular text generations don't hit it.

rory (Py SDK): That points to our retry path reconstructing the request but not reapplying the auth hook for async retries. We attach Authorization in an async hook that mutates headers; if the retry clones a Request object without re-running hooks, header can be missing.

zane (Backend): We also changed the streaming boundary handling last sprint to allow partial outputs for continuous batching. If the client retries mid-stream the concatenation could happen server-side, but auth being missing on the retry is definitely a client bug.

rory (Py SDK): Short-term workaround: set the header on the session explicitly: `client._session.headers.update({'Authorization': f'Bearer {KEY}'})` before calling fn_call, or disable auto-retries for fn_call via config. Not great, I know.

alana (DevEx): confirmed setting session header eliminated the second unauth'd request locally. UX impact though for customers following quickstart.

nina (QA): logs for the JSON error: `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Extra data: line 1 column 512 (char 511)` — body contained two JSON blobs back-to-back.

rory (Py SDK): I'll open an issue and push a fix to ensure hooks run when building retry requests for async flows. Also will add a test that simulates header-less retry and asserts we never send a retry without auth.

zane (Backend): Good. Also adding a safeguard server-side: if we detect two top-level JSON objects concatenated, return a special error code to make client-side debugging clearer.

rory (Py SDK): Filed ticket: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/issues/1212 — "async fn_call retry may omit Authorization header -> duplicated tool output parse errors". Working on a small patch to reapply auth hook in retry builder and added CI test.

alana (DevEx): can you add a tiny note to the upgrade guide / quickstart docs so customers know the temporary workaround until the patch ships? We hit at least two onboarding customers with this.

rory (Py SDK): Yep. I'll add changelog entry and a short troubleshooting snippet. Planning to backport to 0.12.x as a patch.

ci-bot: CI started for branch fix/retry-async-auth-1212.

nina (QA): after rory's local patch, I re-ran repro and only a single tool request appears. parsing OK. :white_check_mark:

alana (DevEx): thanks all 44d leaving thread here for docs follow-up.
